findings.title: RequireAdmin logic always rejects - condition is always true
findings.description: The condition `s.Role != "admin" || s.Role != "owner"` is always true because a role cannot be both admin and owner simultaneously. This means no user can ever pass the admin check, even legitimate admins/owners.

findings.title: BearerToken panics on missing or malformed Authorization header
findings.description: The function assumes the header exists and contains a space, then accesses parts[1] without bounds checking. Missing, empty, or malformed headers cause index out of range panic.

findings.title: Verify does O(n) linear search instead of O(1) map lookup
findings.description: The sessions map is keyed by token, but Verify iterates all values comparing s.Token == token instead of using direct map access a.sessions[token].

findings.title: Token leaked in error response
findings.description: The unauthorized error response includes the raw token in the message body, exposing it to the client.

findings.title: Get modifies map and counters under read lock (data races)
findings.description: Get holds RLock but calls delete(c.m, code), modifies e.used, and increments c.hits - all data races. Go maps cannot be modified under read lock.

findings.title: evict calls Get while holding write lock (deadlock)
findings.description: evict is called with write lock held (line 64), but calls c.Get which tries to acquire read lock, causing deadlock.

findings.title: Delete doesn't stop timer, causing timer leak and double-delete
findings.description: Timer in c.timers[code] continues to fire after Delete, calling Delete again on already-removed key. Timer not stopped or removed from timers map.

findings.title: Peek has no locking (concurrent map access race)
findings.description: Peek accesses c.m without any lock while Set/Delete modify it with write lock, causing data race.

findings.title: Stats has data race on hits counter
findings.description: Stats returns c.hits without locking while Get increments it under read lock (already racy). Concurrent access causes data race.

findings.title: Warm has TOCTOU race between Peek and Set
findings.description: Warm checks Peek(code) without lock, then calls Set. Another goroutine can insert the same key between Peek and Set.

findings.title: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS parsed as seconds not milliseconds
findings.description: Environment variable name indicates milliseconds (_MS) but code multiplies by time.Second instead of time.Millisecond, making TTL 1000x longer than configured.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT parsed but never assigned to config
findings.description: Parsed limit value is assigned to blank identifier `_ = limit` instead of `cfg.FetchLimit = limit`, so the config value never changes from default.

findings.title: Validate always returns nil even when validation fails
findings.description: Validation errors are collected and logged but the function returns nil, so callers cannot detect invalid configuration.

findings.title: ExportCSV uses world-readable 0666 permissions despite comment saying private
findings.description: Comment states report is for service user only, but 0666 allows world read. Sensitive data (all owners' links) exposed to other users on system.

findings.title: WriteSnapshot doesn't check os.Rename error; cross-device rename fails silently
findings.description: os.Rename across filesystems (e.g., /tmp to /var) fails but error is ignored. Temp file left in /tmp, snapshot not written to target dir.

findings.title: redirect lowercases code but store uses case-sensitive keys
findings.description: Code is generated via base64url (case-sensitive) but redirect converts to lowercase before lookup, breaking resolution for codes with uppercase letters.

findings.title: deleteLink missing ownership check - any user can delete any link
findings.description: Comment says only creator can delete, but handler calls store.Delete(code) without verifying the authenticated owner matches link owner.

findings.title: adminQuotas checks X-Admin header that is never set
findings.description: Authenticator middleware sets X-Owner, not X-Admin. No code path sets X-Admin, so admin endpoint is always forbidden.

findings.title: Division by zero panic in stats when no links exist
findings.description: hits / int64(len(links)) panics when len(links) == 0 because division by zero.

findings.title: Resolve expiry check logic inverted - deletes valid links
findings.description: Condition `time.Now().Before(l.ExpiresAt)` is true when link is NOT expired, but code deletes it and returns NotFound. Valid links are treated as expired.

findings.title: Rename validates 'from' twice, never validates 'to'
findings.description: Second validateCode call uses 'from' instead of 'to', so destination code is never validated for length/character constraints.

findings.title: Page has off-by-one error causing panic on last page
findings.description: When end > len(all), code sets end = len(all) + 1, causing slice bounds out of range panic on return all[offset:end].

findings.title: SuccessRate integer division order wrong - always returns 0 for partial success
findings.description: `used / len(s.links) * 100` does integer division first (yielding 0 when used < len), then multiplies by 100. Should multiply first.

findings.title: Delete doesn't decrement quota - users can't recreate after delete
findings.description: Quota map is incremented on Create but never decremented on Delete. Owner variable is read but ignored (_ = l.Owner).

findings.title: Top sorts ascending (least hits first) but comment says most hits first
findings.description: sort.Slice uses `all[i].Hits < all[j].Hits` which sorts ascending. Comment and method name imply descending order.

findings.title: ByOwner uses substring match instead of exact match
findings.description: `strings.Contains(l.Owner, owner)` matches partial strings - owner "alice" matches "alicebob". Should be exact equality.

findings.title: Extend sets expiry from now instead of extending current expiry
findings.description: `l.ExpiresAt = time.Now().Add(ttl)` resets expiry to now+ttl rather than adding ttl to existing expiry. A link expiring in 1 day extended by 7 days gets only 7 days total, not 8.

findings.title: Quotas returns internal map directly, not a snapshot
findings.description: Function returns s.quota directly allowing callers to mutate store's internal state. Comment claims it returns a snapshot.

findings.title: Import not atomic - partial links stored on validation failure
findings.description: Comment says 'either every link in the batch is stored, or none of them is', but validation failure after some inserts leaves those links in store.

findings.title: Prune returns remaining count instead of removed count
findings.description: Function increments `removed` counter but returns `len(s.links)` (remaining count) instead of `removed`.

findings.title: AddResolved uses value receiver - mutex locks copy, no synchronization
findings.description: Method signature `func (m Metrics) AddResolved()` copies the struct; mutex operations lock the copy, providing no actual thread safety.

findings.title: StartJanitor accesses store.links without locking (data race with HTTP handlers)
findings.description: Janitor goroutine iterates and deletes from s.links map concurrently with HTTP handlers that also access the map. Store has no mutex.

findings.title: WarmCache wg.Add(1) inside goroutine races with wg.Wait()
findings.description: wg.Add(1) called after goroutine starts; wg.Wait() may return before Add executes, causing premature exit or panic.

findings.title: CheckTargets goroutine leak on early error return
findings.description: When first error received, function returns but remaining goroutines block forever trying to send to unbuffered results channel with no receiver.

findings.title: mustHead returns nil request on error causing panic in caller
findings.description: When http.NewRequest fails, req is nil but function returns it anyway. Caller client.Do(nil) panics.

findings.title: Authenticator.sessions map has no synchronization
findings.description: Authenticator.sessions map is accessed concurrently by Issue(), Verify(), Revoke(), and Middleware() without any mutex, causing data races on every operation.

findings.title: Metrics.AddResolved uses value receiver, mutex copied
findings.description: Metrics.AddResolved() uses a value receiver, causing the sync.Mutex to be copied on each call. The lock protects nothing; resolved counter has a data race.

findings.title: Store.links map has no synchronization
findings.description: Store.links and Store.quota maps are accessed by all Store methods and the janitor goroutine without any mutex, causing pervasive data races.

findings.title: Cache.evict calls Get while holding write lock, deadlocks
findings.description: Cache.evict() calls c.Get() while the caller (Set) holds the write lock. Get() attempts to acquire RLock(), which blocks forever because the write lock is held.

findings.title: Cache.Get mutates map and counters under RLock
findings.description: Cache.Get() modifies e.used, increments c.hits, and deletes from c.m while holding only RLock(). This violates RWMutex contract and causes data races with concurrent writers and other readers.

findings.title: Cache.Peek accesses map without lock
findings.description: Cache.Peek() reads c.m without acquiring any lock, racing with concurrent writes from Set, Get, Delete, and evict.

findings.title: Cache.Stats reads hits counter without lock
findings.description: Cache.Stats() reads c.hits without synchronization while Get() writes it under RLock, causing a data race.

findings.title: Cache.Set timer can delete wrong entry after code reuse
findings.description: Timer created in Set captures 'code' variable. If entry is removed and code reused, the stale timer deletes the new entry.

findings.title: Cache.Delete doesn't clean up timer, double-delete risk
findings.description: Cache.Delete() doesn't remove the timer from c.timers, so the timer fires later and calls Delete on a potentially non-existent key. Also has a TOCTOU between existence check and delete.

findings.title: StartJanitor accesses Store.links without lock
findings.description: The janitor goroutine iterates and deletes from s.links without synchronization, racing with all Store methods that access the same map.

findings.title: WarmCache wg.Add inside goroutine causes hang on panic
findings.description: wg.Add(1) is called inside the spawned goroutine. If the goroutine exits early (error return) before reaching wg.Add(1), the WaitGroup never accounts for it and wg.Wait() blocks indefinitely.

findings.title: CheckTargets goroutine leak on early return
findings.description: CheckTargets spawns N goroutines but only receives N results. If it returns early on first error, remaining goroutines block forever sending to the unbuffered channel.

findings.title: Store.Quotas returns internal map reference
findings.description: Store.Quotas() returns the internal quota map directly, allowing external mutation without synchronization.

findings.title: Store returns internal Link pointers to callers
findings.description: Store.Page(), Top(), ByOwner() return *Link pointers that alias the store's internal data. Callers can mutate Link fields concurrently with store operations.

findings.title: Store.Delete doesn't decrement quota
findings.description: Store.Delete() has '_ = l.Owner' but doesn't decrement the owner's quota. Quota map overcounts permanently. Also no lock on quota map.

findings.title: Store.Import doesn't update quota, no conflict check
findings.description: Store.Import() writes links to the map without checking for code conflicts with existing entries and doesn't update the quota map. No synchronization.

findings.title: Store.Prune returns wrong count
findings.description: Store.Prune() computes 'removed' but returns len(s.links) instead. Bug but not a concurrency issue per se.

findings.title: RequireAdmin logic always rejects
findings.description: RequireAdmin uses || instead of &&, so it rejects all roles including admin and owner. Logic error: should be 's.Role != "admin" && s.Role != "owner"'.

findings.title: BearerToken panics on malformed header
findings.description: BearerToken assumes Authorization header has format 'Bearer <token>' and accesses parts[1] without bounds check. Malformed header causes panic.

findings.title: SSRF in preview handler - fetches user-controlled URLs without validation
findings.description: The preview handler (line 89-108) resolves a user-supplied code to a target URL and makes an HTTP GET request to it. The target comes from the store which only validates it's an http/https URL, but does not block internal addresses (localhost, 169.254.169.254, private RFC1918 ranges). An attacker can create a short link pointing to internal services and use /preview to probe or exfiltrate data from the internal network.

findings.title: Open redirect in /out endpoint via unvalidated 'next' parameter
findings.description: The /out handler (line 144-152) redirects to any URL provided in the 'next' query parameter with no validation. This allows attackers to craft links that appear to go to the linkd service but redirect victims to phishing or malware sites. The redirect uses 301 (MovedPermanently) which browsers may cache.

findings.title: SSRF in WarmCache and CheckTargets - fetches arbitrary user-controlled URLs
findings.description: WarmCache (line 64-82) and CheckTargets (line 86-105) make HTTP HEAD requests to all link targets in the store. Since users control the target URLs when creating links, this provides an SSRF vector to scan internal networks. These run in background goroutines with the same privileges as the main server.

findings.title: Session tokens generated with math/rand instead of crypto/rand
findings.description: The Issue function (line 41-55) uses math/rand.Intn(256) to generate 16-byte session tokens. math/rand is not cryptographically secure - its output is predictable if an attacker can observe enough tokens or determine the seed. This allows session hijacking.

findings.title: Password hashing uses unsalted SHA-256 - vulnerable to rainbow tables
findings.description: HashPassword (line 69-72) computes a plain SHA-256 hash of the password with no salt and no key stretching. This is vulnerable to rainbow table attacks, GPU brute-forcing, and identical passwords produce identical hashes. Not suitable for password storage.

findings.title: RequireAdmin logic bug - always denies access even for admins
findings.description: RequireAdmin (line 83-87) checks `if s.Role != "admin" || s.Role != "owner"`. This condition is always true because a role cannot be both 'admin' AND 'owner' simultaneously. The || should be &&. This breaks admin functionality entirely.

findings.title: Session tokens logged in plaintext
findings.description: Line 53 logs the full session token: [REDACTED]"auth: issued token %s for %s", s.Token, owner)`. Tokens in logs can be exposed via log aggregation systems, debug endpoints, or accidental log sharing.

findings.title: Token leaked in error response
findings.description: Middleware (line 96) includes the token in the error message: `http.Error(w, "unauthorized: "+err.Error()+" (token "+token+")", ...)`. This exposes valid/invalid tokens to anyone making requests, aiding token enumeration or debugging by attackers.

findings.title: CORS misconfiguration - wildcard origin with credentials
findings.description: writeJSON (line 193-194) sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` together. This combination is invalid per CORS spec (wildcard cannot be used with credentials) and causes browsers to reject the response, but more importantly indicates confused security posture. If credentials are needed, the origin must be explicitly validated and echoed.

findings.title: Admin endpoint protected only by easily-spoofed header
findings.description: adminQuotas (line 155-161) checks for `X-Admin: true` header. Any client can set this header - it provides no real authentication. Should use the authenticator's session/role system like other endpoints.

findings.title: Resolve deletes non-expired links due to inverted expiration check
findings.description: Resolve (line 60-71) checks `if time.Now().Before(l.ExpiresAt)` and if true, deletes the link and returns NotFound. This is backwards - it deletes links that HAVE NOT YET EXPIRED. Valid links are destroyed on first access.

findings.title: Metrics.AddResolved uses value receiver - mutex operates on copy, no synchronization
findings.description: AddResolved (line 20-24) has receiver `m Metrics` (value) not `*Metrics` (pointer). The mutex lock/unlock operates on a copy of the struct, providing no actual thread safety. Concurrent increments of resolved are lost/raced.

findings.title: Hardcoded weak default secret for session signing
findings.description: NewAuthenticator (line 30-33) uses "dev-secret-do-not-use" as fallback if LINKD_SECRET env var is not set. This secret is known and constant across all deployments that don't configure the env var, allowing token forgery.

findings.title: BearerToken panics on missing or malformed Authorization header
findings.description: BearerToken (line 75-79) splits the header on space and returns parts[1] without checking length. If header is missing, empty, or doesn't contain a space, this causes index out of range panic, leading to DoS via nil pointer dereference in middleware.

findings.title: Data race in Cache.Get - modifies entry under read lock
findings.description: Get (line 36-50) holds RLock but modifies `e.used = time.Now()` (line 47) and increments `c.hits++` (line 48). The entry is a pointer shared across goroutines; concurrent reads and writes to the same fields cause data races.

findings.title: Cache TTL parsed as seconds but env var is documented as milliseconds
findings.description: LoadConfig (line 51-56) reads LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS (milliseconds per comment) but multiplies by time.Second instead of time.Millisecond. This makes TTL 1000x longer than configured, potentially causing stale cache entries.

findings.title: Validate() returns nil even when configuration is invalid
findings.description: Validate (line 102-117) collects problems but always returns nil. Callers cannot detect invalid configuration, so bad deployments start successfully and fail at runtime.

findings.title: Path traversal in ExportCSV via user-controlled filename
findings.description: ExportCSV (line 12-30) uses `filepath.Join(dir, name+".csv")` where name comes from user input (main.go:181). filepath.Join does not prevent directory traversal if name contains `..` (e.g., `../../etc/passwd`). The comment claims it's confined to dir but this is false.

findings.title: Path traversal in ArchiveAll via owner-controlled filename
findings.description: ArchiveAll (line 34-46) uses `filepath.Base(owner)` for the filename. While filepath.Base strips directory components, owner comes from user input during link creation and could contain problematic characters. Also, the export directory is user-configurable via config.

findings.title: Exported CSV files created with world-readable permissions (0666)
findings.description: ExportCSV (line 26) writes files with mode 0666 (world read/write). These files contain all users' link data. Any user on the system can read/modify them.

findings.title: Snapshot temp file created in world-writable /tmp - symlink attack risk
findings.description: WriteSnapshot (line 51-62) uses os.CreateTemp("/tmp", ...). An attacker with local access could create a symlink at the predictable temp path pointing to a sensitive file, causing the rename to overwrite it.

findings.title: ByOwner uses substring match - leaks other users' links
findings.description: ByOwner (line 156-164) uses `strings.Contains(l.Owner, owner)` which matches substrings. An owner named "alice" would see links owned by "alice2", "malice", etc. This violates isolation between users.

findings.title: Quotas returns internal map - caller can mutate store state
findings.description: Quotas (line 179-181) returns the internal `s.quota` map directly. Callers can modify the map, corrupting the store's quota tracking.

findings.title: Rename validates 'from' code twice instead of validating 'to'
findings.description: Rename (line 74-92) calls validateCode(from) twice (lines 75 and 78) and never validates the 'to' code. A malicious 'to' code with invalid characters could be injected.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT parsed but discarded
findings.description: LoadConfig (line 65-70) parses LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT but assigns to `_` (blank identifier), so the value is never used. The config field FetchLimit remains at default.

findings.title: Prune returns remaining count instead of removed count
findings.description: Prune (line 197-206) tracks removed in variable but returns `len(s.links)` (remaining) instead of `removed`. Callers expecting removed count get wrong value.
